best_for: People building a large personal wiki who want nested notes, scripting and their own sync server instead of a hosted notes service.
description:
Trilium Notes is a note-taking app for building a large personal knowledge base, made by the TriliumNext community from the original work of developer zadam. It is free and open source under the AGPL-3.0.

You can lock single notes with a password so they stay encrypted, and Trilium keeps older versions of each note in case you need to go back. Full-text search finds any note, and you can focus on one branch of the tree and hide the rest. Moving in is easy: it imports from Evernote and reads and writes Markdown. A web clipper saves pages from your browser, and you can publish chosen notes to the public web for others to read.

points.title: Free and self-hosted
points.text: Trilium is open source under AGPL-3.0, with no paid plan. To sync between computers you run your own Trilium server, for example from the Docker image.

points.title: A tree that scales
points.text: Notes sit in a deep tree, and one note can appear in several places through cloning. The project says it handles over 100,000 notes.

points.title: More than text notes
points.text: Besides a rich editor with tables and math, it has code notes, Excalidraw canvases, mind maps, note maps and geo maps. Attributes, scripting and a REST API let you automate it.

points.title: No official phone app
points.text: On a phone you use the mobile web view of your server. Native apps for Android and iOS exist, but they come from third parties.

points.title: Now run by TriliumNext
points.text: The original author handed the project to the TriliumNext community. Your old database still works, but versions after 0.90.4 cannot sync with zadam's 0.63.7 or older.

points.title: Install details
points.text: The Windows installer is per-user, for x64 and Arm64. Mac builds need macOS 13 or later. The Flathub package is verified for the Trilium Notes Team, for x64 and Arm64.

points.title: Downgrades on Windows
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 33 versions. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so going back there needs another source.
